another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I do. I have a child - Alex, who is 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know you have Alex, who is 13 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you don't currently live in the UK, I need to understand your specific situation as there are some circumstances where you might still be eligible for Child Benefit even when living abroad.

Can you tell me which country you're currently living in?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad at the moment, outside the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand you're living abroad. To help determine if you might still be eligible for Child Benefit, I need to know a bit more about your circumstances.

Are you (or your partner, if applicable) a Crown servant - meaning do you work for the UK government, diplomatic service, or armed forces while abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant and I don't work for the UK government, diplomatic service, or armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

Based on the information you've provided:
- You have Alex, who is 13 years old
- You live outside the UK
- You are not a Crown servant or working for the UK government, diplomatic service, or armed forces abroad

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally need to live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit. There are exceptions for Crown servants and those living in certain specific countries, but since you've confirmed you're not a Crown servant and you're living abroad outside the UK, this would generally mean you wouldn't qualify for Child Benefit.

Just to be thorough - are you living in an EEA (European Economic Area) country or Switzerland, or do you have any other specific connection to the UK (such as being temporarily abroad for a specific purpose)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have any other specific connection like that. I'm just living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would be **ineligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

While Alex is 13 years old and meets the age requirement (under 16), the fundamental rule for Child Benefit is that you must live in the UK. The main exceptions to this rule are for:
- Crown servants (UK government workers, diplomatic service, or armed forces abroad)
- Those living in certain specific countries with particular agreements

Since you've confirmed that you're living abroad and don't fall into any of these exception categories, you don't meet the residence requirement for Child Benefit.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you move back to the UK - you would be able to claim Child Benefit at that time, as long as Alex is still under 16 (or under 20 if in approved education or training).

Is there anything else I can help clarify about Child Benefit?
